🎬 When the Game Stands Tall (2014)

When the Game Stands Tall tells the inspiring true story of the De La Salle High School football team in Concord, California, whose extraordinary 151-game winning streak becomes one of the most remarkable achievements in American sports history. Under the leadership of dedicated head coach Bob Ladouceur, the team develops a powerful reputation built on discipline, teamwork, commitment, and a philosophy that emphasizes character over individual success. However, after years of dominating opponents and setting records, the Spartans face an unexpected defeat that brings their legendary winning streak to an end. As players struggle with disappointment, pressure, and uncertainty, the team must confront difficult questions about their identity and what truly defines greatness. Meanwhile, Coach Ladouceur faces personal health challenges and emotional struggles that force him to reconsider his priorities both on and off the football field. As the players deal with family problems, personal tragedies, and the expectations of their community, they begin learning that success involves far more than winning games. Through demanding practices, emotional conversations, intense rivalries, and unforgettable football moments, the team gradually discovers the importance of unity, resilience, and supporting one another during difficult times. Combining powerful sports drama, emotional storytelling, inspiring performances, and meaningful life lessons, the film explores leadership, brotherhood, perseverance, humility, faith, and the true meaning of victory.

🎭 Genre: Sports • Drama • Biography

⭐ IMDb: 6.6/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 55m • PG

🎥 Director: Thomas Carter

source_details.synopsis: When the Game Stands Tall is a 2014 American sports drama film directed by Thomas Carter. The plot concerns a record 151-game 1992–2003 high school football winning streak by De La Salle High School of Concord, California. It stars Jim Caviezel as coach Bob Ladouceur, Laura Dern as Bev Ladouceur, Michael Chiklis as assistant coach Terry Eidson and Alexander Ludwig as running back Chris Ryan. The film is an adaptation of the 2003 book of the same name by Neil Hayes, published by North Atlantic Books. De La Salle head coach Bob Ladouceur retired in January 2013 after winning his last Open Division state championship in December 2012. The film was released on August 22, 2014.
